passages.original: Quod enim Esaias iaculatur in suggillatione haereticorum ipsorum, et inprimis, Vae qui faciunt dulce amarum et tenebras lucem, istos scilicet notat qui nec vocabula ista in luce proprietatum suarum conservant, ut anima non alia sit quam quae vocatur, et caro non alia quam quae videtur, et deus non alius quam qui praedicatur. Ideo etiam Marcionem prospiciens, Ego sum, inquit, deus, et alius absque me non est. Et cum alias id ipsum eodem modo dicit, Ante me deus non fuit, nescio quas illas Valentinianorum Aconum genealogias pulsat. Et, Non ex sanguine neque ex carnis et viri voluntate, sed ex deo natus est, Hebioni respondit.
passages.english: For what Isaiah hurls in rebuke of the heretics themselves, and above all, "Woe to those who make sweet bitter and darkness light," marks, of course, those who do not keep even these words in the light of their proper meanings, so that the soul is nothing other than what it is called, and the flesh nothing other than what is seen, and God nothing other than the one who is proclaimed. Therefore also, foreseeing Marcion, he says, "I am God, and there is no other besides me." And when elsewhere he says the very same thing in the same way, "Before me there was no god," he strikes at those genealogies, whatever they are, of the Aeons of the Valentinians. And [the saying], "He was born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh and of a man, but of God," answered Ebion.
passages.notes: "Aconum" is a scanning error for "Aeonum" (Aeons). "Hebioni" is Ebion, the supposed founder of the Ebionites. The Isaiah quotation is loosely cited: the original pairs "sweet bitter" and "darkness light" in a compressed form.
